This initiative focuses on four key pillars: reshaping theCustoms-Port-Trade (CPT) Single Window for better collaboration,developing intelligent services through data analytics, adopting cloudcomputing for operational flexibility, and strengthening cybersecurityand off-site backups.As a critical national infrastructure, the program aims to acceleratedigital transformation, creating a resilient and smart customs environmentthat supports Taiwan’s long-term economic development and internationaltrade efficiency. Following China’s new trade measures, Taiwan’s Ministry of Agriculturereaffirmed its strategy to diversify export markets and reduce relianceon an unpredictable Chinese market. Taiwan has successfully shiftedfocus to Japan, Singapore, and North America.Notably, fruit and vegetable exports to China plummeted from 73% in2019 to just 12.6% last year, with Japan now the top buyer of Taiwanesepineapples. While open to resuming trade, Taiwan remains cautious,prioritizing scientific management and improved cold-chain systems toensure long-term quality and stability in global markets.
